claims.statement: For a differentiable event time t(theta) crossing the finite trial boundary T transversely, the hard per-event cost c*1{0<=t(theta)<T}, c>0, is discontinuous at the crossing even if t(theta) is continuous.
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty or priority claim. The proposition is an elementary objective/interface consequence; full prior-art review is incomplete.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample under the stated scalar transverse-crossing assumptions, or discovery that the claimed objective uses a continuous event cost rather than a hard finite-window count.
claims.next_gate: Check the precise training energy objective in prior exact-gradient SNN work and in any selected device implementation.

claims.statement: If event timing is t(theta)+eta, eta~Normal(0,sigma^2) with fixed sigma>0, then the expected per-event energy inside [0,T) is c[Phi((T-t(theta))/sigma)-Phi(-t(theta)/sigma)] and has derivative c/sigma*[phi(t/sigma)-phi((T-t)/sigma)]*t'(theta).
assumptions: additive independent Gaussian timing error for this event
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty or priority claim; direct expected-value smoothing is elementary and related stochastic event-gradient prior art exists. Device relevance is unknown.
costs: Requires measured sigma and event energy; repeat-calibration cost unknown.
Gradient magnitude near T can scale as c*abs(t')/(sigma*sqrt(2*pi)); poor small-sigma conditioning remains.
No device training or acquisition cost measured.
claims.falsifier: On held-out repeated trials, fitted Gaussian jitter fails to predict event-in-window probabilities or measured energy; or calibrated objective fails to reduce measured event energy at matched task quality.
claims.next_gate: A blinded device experiment with calibration/validation split, task-loss-only QIF control, hard-count comparator, and matched-accuracy/margin outcomes.
